decisions.reason: The XL package was publicly launched as a first-time capability for large practices, costs little to maintain as an extension of the established anamnesis app, and fits the firm's announced paperless direction, so persisting is the natural choice.

The materials management module builds on the core practice software and the firm has invested in developing it; with only a single year on the market, weak uptake can still be attributed to the normal ramp-up period, so management keeps it.

The KIM messaging client is tied to mandatory telematics infrastructure, has a dedicated page and update announcements, and is central to the firm's integrated health-IT direction, so dropping it is very unlikely.
